lessons.title: Introduction to Flask

content.title: What is Flask?
content.text: Flask is a lightweight Python web framework used to build web applications and APIs.

content.title: First Flask Application
Development Server
content.text: The Flask development server allows you to run and test an application locally during development.

key_points: Flask is a Python web framework.
Flask applications are commonly created using Flask(__name__).

lessons.title: Routes and Views

content.title: Routes
content.text: A route connects a URL path to a Python function. When a user visits that URL, Flask calls the associated function.

content.title: Multiple Routes
Dynamic Routes
content.text: Flask can capture values directly from a URL and pass them to the view function.

content.title: HTTP Methods
content.text: Routes can handle HTTP methods such as GET and POST.

key_points: Dynamic routes can capture URL values.
GET is commonly used to retrieve data.
POST is commonly used to submit data.

content.title: Flask Templates
content.text: Flask uses the Jinja template engine to generate dynamic HTML pages.

content.title: Rendering a Template
Template Condition
Template Loop

lessons.title: Forms and Request Data

content.title: Handling Forms
content.text: Flask provides the request object for accessing information submitted by users.

content.title: Reading Form Data
GET Parameters
content.text: Query-string parameters can be accessed using request.args.

content.title: Query Parameter
Validation
content.text: Applications should validate submitted input before processing or storing it.

key_points: request provides access to incoming request data.

lessons.title: Building JSON APIs

content.title: Flask APIs
content.text: Flask can be used to build APIs that return JSON data to frontend applications or other clients.

content.title: JSON Response
REST Concepts
content.text: REST APIs commonly use HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT and DELETE to work with resources.

content.title: POST API

lessons.title: Databases and Application Data

content.title: Database Integration
content.text: Flask applications can connect to databases such as SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL.

content.title: SQLAlchemy
content.text: SQLAlchemy is a popular Python SQL toolkit and ORM that can be used with Flask applications.

content.title: Simple SQLite Connection
content.code:
import sqlite3

connection = sqlite3.connect('app.db')
cursor = connection.cursor()
cursor.execute('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)')
connection.commit()
connection.close()

content.title: Why Use an ORM?
content.text: An ORM allows application code to work with database records through programming-language objects rather than manually writing every SQL statement.

key_points: Flask can work with many databases.
SQLite is useful for small applications and development.
SQLAlchemy provides SQL and ORM functionality.
Database connections should be handled carefully.

lessons.title: Project Structure and Best Practices

content.title: Project Structure
content.text: As Flask applications grow, separating routes, templates, static files, models and configuration makes the project easier to maintain.

content.title: Blueprints
content.text: Blueprints allow related routes and functionality to be organized into reusable components.

content.title: Blueprint Example
Environment Variables
content.text: Secrets such as API keys and database credentials should be stored in environment variables instead of being hard-coded in source files.

key_points: Large Flask applications benefit from modular structure.
Configuration should be separated from application logic.
